# qbittorrent_category (Resource)

Manage one download category. Import by name. Rename replaces the category. Destroy reassigns torrents to the parent category; TMM may relocate data. It does not delete torrents or files. Delete is refused while descendant categories exist; remove them first. Avoid concurrent hierarchy mutations.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "qbittorrent_category" "movies" {
  name      = "movies"
  save_path = "/downloads/movies"
}

# Referencing the parent orders creation and leaf-first deletion.
resource "qbittorrent_category" "kids" {
  name      = "${qbittorrent_category.movies.name}/kids"
  save_path = "" # /downloads/movies/kids, beneath the parent's effective path
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Category name. Slash-separated subcategories require existing ancestors. Reference the parent resource name to order lifecycle operations. Changing this forces replacement.
- `save_path` (String) Save path on the server. An empty path resolves to the category basename beneath its parent effective path (or the default save path for a top-level category). A nonempty relative path resolves beneath the global default save path. Absolute paths are used directly. Use normalized paths.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Category name, used as the resource ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import qbittorrent_category.movies movies
```
